doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The duo piano sessions with John Lewis
summary: After choosing Steinways, Jones and Lewis worked from written arrangements, trading the roles of soloist and accompanist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How about the sessions you did with John Lewis?
They were done in New York. That is the one where we went to the Steinway factory and picked out meticulously, the pianos we wanted to use on the date.

Let’s see, I think it was…who was the A&R man that used to work with John Lewis? What was his name? Names are escaping me right now. I need another night’s sleep. Anyway, the idea came from on high let's say. John and I had known each other for some time and I think the date, musically, came together pretty well. Our ideas were different but they blended well. The one thing you have to remember when you are doing a duo piano player with another pianist is that at times you must be accompanist. You cannot solo 100% of the time. You solo when it is your turn to solo. Then, the other piano player becomes the accompanist. If you both try to solo at the same time, it results in what we know in the business as a train wreck.

How did you prepare for those duet dates? I mean, you talked about finding the pianos and so forth, but how did you decide that you were going to do this piece or that piece? Did a lot rehearsal go into it?

We had minimal rehearsal. You know,… Actually, in the case of John and I, as opposed to the case of Tommy and I… I have done a couple of duos. I have also done quartet. I have done a couple of quartet piano things. In most cases, if you are doing a piano duo thing, if things are really written now, if the arrangement is really written out in every pianist has a part to play, then things are a little more

organized. Actually, they are a lot more organized and it sounds that way. Therefore, you don't have the harmonic problems that you would have if you were doing it just off the top of your head. John was very meticulous. In addition to being a good band arranger, he is also a good arranger for two pianos too. The date we did, many of the things were written out. I think I may have only been one or two things we did not have music for. It was highly organized and that showed.
Well written out but leaving some space for improvisation.

Well, of course when one pianist would be the accompanist, we would be playing comp below them. Then, the other player is playing the solo as part of the arrangement. John left room for each of us to play as much solo as we wanted to.
